paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.

model_annotations.English: The chart titled “QAdapter” illustrates the computational cost, shown as floating-point operations, for several fine-tuning approaches listed along the category axis. The horizontal axis contains the method categories (rotated diagonal text) in the order: Full FT, TAG, Adapter, MTL-FT, Q-Adapter, and Ours. The vertical axis is labeled “# FLOPs” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick labels at approximately \(10^{18}\), \(10^{19}\), and \(10^{20}\), spanning roughly from just under \(10^{18}\) up to \(10^{20}\). Each category is represented by a single solid bar: Full FT is an orange bar reaching to about \(6\times 10^{19}\); TAG is orange at roughly \(2\times 10^{19}\); Adapter is orange at around \(1.6\times 10^{19}\); MTL-FT is orange at approximately \(3.5\times 10^{18}\); Q-Adapter is orange near about \(1.8\times 10^{18}\); and Ours is a green bar at roughly \(2\times 10^{18}\). The bars appear arranged from higher to lower values from left to right through Q-Adapter, with the final “Ours” bar distinctly colored green for emphasis compared with the orange baseline bars, and there are no stacked/grouped components or numeric annotations on individual bars.
model_annotations.German: The chart titled “QAdapter” illustrates a comparison of computational cost across several fine-tuning approaches using a single series of vertical bars representing the number of floating-point operations. The horizontal axis contains the categorical methods, shown left to right as “Full FT,” “TAG,” “Adapter,” “MTL-FT,” “Q-Adapter,” and “Ours,” with the category labels rotated diagonally; “Ours” is additionally visually emphasized by bold text. The vertical axis is the value axis labeled “# FLOPs,” displayed on a logarithmic scale with major tick labels at approximately \(10^{18}\), \(10^{19}\), and \(10^{20}\), spanning roughly from just under \(10^{18}\) up to slightly above \(10^{20}\). Each category has one bar: “Full FT” is an orange bar reaching around \(6\times10^{19}\); “TAG” is orange at roughly \(2\times10^{19}\); “Adapter” is orange near \(1.6\text{–}1.8\times10^{19}\); “MTL-FT” is orange around \(3\text{–}4\times10^{18}\); “Q-Adapter” is orange around \(1.7\text{–}2.0\times10^{18}\); and “Ours” is a green bar around \(2\times10^{18}\). The bars are not grouped or stacked, there is no legend shown, and the categories appear arranged from higher bars on the left toward lower bars to the right, with the final “Ours” bar distinguished by its green color.
